A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSQAD study and contain 24 pages, including Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support matching all sections, equations, figures and tables without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-language and cross-model experiments in Sections 4–5, plus question-quality, translation-quality and human-rating results in Appendices A and C.

after.justification: v2 reports the same original empirical outcomes, including language-pair statistical tests, evaluations of six additional LLMs and human assessments.

M1.justification: The question-generation and selection pipeline, multilingual response prompts, refusal detection and embedding-based analyses remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A, B and E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 17 Human Rights Watch topics and six languages: English, Korean, Chinese, Spanish, German and Hindi. Coverage of acceptable and non-acceptable responses is unchanged.

E2.justification: Section 5 and Figures 6–7 retain the same evaluated models: Gemma, Llama-2, Llama-3, Mistral-v0.2, Phi-3-mini and Qwen-1.5. No comparator is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: The data-selection thresholds, refusal-classification procedure, controlled variables, model configurations and human/translation evaluation samples remain unchanged in Appendices A–D. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The selection-threshold comparison in Table 4, validation analyses in Tables 2, 5 and 6, and multilingual/model case studies in Appendix F are retained. Correcting the German label does not change the case-study evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same significance testing, permutation-test formulation, standard-deviation reporting and Krippendorff’s alpha analysis. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Appendix C.1 still reports acceptance of the McNemar null in 11 of 255 comparisons (4.31%). Changing 'Chinse-English' to 'Chinese-English' corrects spelling without changing the reported language pair or finding.

T1.justification: The hypotheses, definitions and mathematical formulations of McNemar’s test and PERMANOVA, including Equations 1–5, remain unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1 contributions and Section 6 conclusion retain the same claims about introducing MSQAD and identifying language- and model-dependent ethical biases through statistical tests.

C2.justification: Interpretations of refusal and informativeness differences are unchanged. The limitations concerning fixed controls, generated-data bias, response quality and six-language coverage also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The model identifiers, translation service, preprocessing details, vLLM implementation and prompt templates remain unchanged. The MSQAD repository disclosure and substantive resource-access information are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. Neither the cited research nor the positioning relative to earlier bias datasets and multilingual studies is revised.

P1.justification: v2 adds the missing article in Figure 1’s caption, corrects 'Chinse-English' and 'Gereman', and changes 'Artificial Intelligent Graduate School Program' to 'Artificial Intelligence Graduate School Program'. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1’s caption is lightly edited and rewrapped, with a few other local line-wrap changes accompanying corrections. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–6 retain their data, arrangement and placement; 20 of the 24 rendered pages are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 makes a few grammatical, spelling and acknowledgment corrections that slightly improve polish. The scientific content, evidence, interpretations, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the appendices, so these copyedits do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
